English Literature.question: ১) Who wrote the poem ‘Tintern Abbey’?
English Literature.exp:
William Wordsworth (1770–1850): English Romantic poet. He is called Poet of Nature, Poet of Childhood, Lake poet.
Major Works: Lyrical Ballad (1798), The Daffodils, The prelude (1850), Lucy poem, Tintern Abbey, The Solitary Reaper, The Excursion.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture]

English Literature.question: ২) Who wrote the pamphlet ‘The Necessity of Atheism’?
English Literature.exp:
Percy Bysshe Shelley (1792 – 1822):
-This English poet was an atheist and expelled from Oxford University in 1811 due to his publication of a pamphlet named “The necessity of Atheism”.
-He believed that only revolution can change our society. So that he is called “Revolutionary Poet”.
-He is also called “The poet of Hope and Regeneration”.
-Shelly mourns over the death of John Keats in his famous elegy “Adonais”.
Famous Books: Prometheus Unbound (1820), Adonais (1821), A Defense of poetry (1820), The Revolt of Islam.
Famous Poems: Ode to the West Wind, To a skylark, Alastor, Ozymandias, Queen Mab, The cloud.
Source: Britannica and LiveMCQ Lecture

English Literature.question: ৩) ‘Lyrical Ballads’ is a collection of romantic poems by-
English Literature.option1: ক) Johan Keats and P.B. Shelley
English Literature.option2: খ) P.B. Shelley and S.T. Coleridge
English Literature.option3: গ) William Wordsworth and S.T. Coleridge
English Literature.option4: ঘ) Lord Byron and William Wordsworth
English Literature.exp:
The Romantic period began in 1798 with the publication of “Lyrical Ballads” is a collection of romantic poems by William Wordsworth and S.T. Coleridge. Revival of Romanticism took place in the Romantic Period.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture and An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman.]

English Literature.question: ৪) Which of the following is the literary work of John Keats?
English Literature.option3: গ) Ode to the west wind
English Literature.exp:
John Keats(1795-1821) English Romantic lyric poet. He is called the Poet of Beauty and also Poet of Sensuousness.
His famous books: Endymion, Hyperion, Lamia.
Famous Poems: Ode to a Nightingale, Ode to Autumn, The Eve of St. Agnes, Ode to Psyche etc.
‘Ode to a Skylark’ and ‘Ode to the west wind’ are famous poems by Percy Bysshe Shelley.
‘Dejection: An ode’ is a famous poem by Samuel Taylor Coleridge.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture and Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question:
৫) ‘To Mercy, Pity, Peace, and Love,
All pray in their distress.’
- is taken from the writings of-
English Literature.exp:
To Mercy, Pity, Peace, and Love
All pray in their distress;
And to these virtues of delight
Return their thankfulness.

For Mercy, Pity, Peace, and Love
Is God, our father dear, And Mercy, Pity, Peace, and Love
Is Man, his child and care.

Source: ‘The Divine Image’ by William Blake.

The Divine Image is part of Songs of Innocence.

English Literature.question: ৬) Who wrote ‘The Essays of Elia’?
English Literature.exp:
Charles Lamb (1775-1834): He was an English Poet and Essayist.
’The Essays of Elia’, ‘The Last Essays of Elia’, ‘Tales from Shakespeare’ etc his famous Essays.
‘The Old Familiar Faces’ is his famous poem.
[Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ lecture.]

English Literature.question: ৭) Who is known as the ‘Poet of Supernaturalism’?
English Literature.exp:
Samuel Taylor Coleridge (1772–1834): He is called the “poet of Supernaturalism”. He is also called the “Lake poet” and “Opium Eater”.
Major works: Biographia Literaria (1833) (prose), The Rime of Ancient Mariner (1798), Kubla Khan, Christabel, Dejection: An ode.
Source: LiveMCQ Lecture and Boston University Library website.

English Literature.question: ৮) Who wrote the novel 'A Tale of Two Cities'?
English Literature.exp:
Charles Dickens is the greatest novelist of the Victorian Period.
Oliver Twist, A Tale of Two Cities, Great Expectations, David Copperfield, Our Mutual Friend, The Christmas Carol, The Bleak House, The Old Curiosity Shop, The Pickwick Papers, Hard Times, The Mystery of Edwin Drood, Little Dorrit, The Battle of Life etc are the famous novel of Charles Dickens.
Jonathan Swift wrote the fiction ‘A Tale of a Tub’ and Ben Johnson wrote the play ‘A Tale of a Tub’.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture and An ABC of English Literature, Dr M Mofizar Rahman]

English Literature.question: ৯) 'Come forth into the light of things, let nature be your teacher.' is taken from the poem of-
English Literature.exp:
'Come forth into the light of things, let nature be your teacher.' is taken from William Wordsworth's poem 'The Tables Turned'.
Other famous quotes of Wordsworth:
- Child the father of man.
- Nature never did betray the heart that loved her.
- Poetry is a spontaneous overflow of powerful feelings.
- Poet is the breath and final speed of knowledge.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture]

English Literature.question: ১০) ‘Don Juan’ is a satirical poem by-
English Literature.exp:
George Gordon Byron / Lord Byron (1788–1824): This English poet revolts against existing social customs and norms. So that he is called “The Rebel Poet”.
Famous books of Byron: The Vision of Judgement, Hours of Idleness, Heaven and Earth.
Famous poem: Childe Harold's Pilgrimage.
Don Juan is a satiric poem by Lord Byron.
[Source: Source: Britannica and LiveMCQ Lecture.]

English Literature.question: ১১) Sir Walter Scott is the writer of -
English Literature.exp:
Sir Walter Scott(1771-1832): Scottish novelist, poet, historian, and biographer who is often considered both the inventor and the greatest practitioner of the historical novel.
‘Ivanhoe’, historical novel by Sir Walter Scott, published in 1819.
His other famous work: Patriotism, The Lady of the Lake(Poem), Talisman(Poem), Waverley etc.
Leo Tolstoy’s novel ‘War and Peace’.
Jane Austen’s novel ‘Emma’, ‘Persuasion’.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica and Live MCQ Lecture]

English Literature.question: ১২) ‘Poverty is the test of civility and the touchstone of friendship.’ was stated by-
English Literature.exp:
‘Poverty is the test of civility and the touchstone of friendship.’-was stated by W. Hazlitt (Characteristics: in the manner of Rochefoucault's Maxims).
His other famous quotes:
-‘We never do anything well till we cease to think about the manner of doing it.’(Sketches and Essays).
-‘The way to procure insults is to submit to them.(Characteristics)’.
-‘A nickname is the hardest stone that the devil can throw at a man.’(Sketches and Essays).
-‘No young man believes he shall ever die.’(Literary Remains).
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ১৩) Who is the author of ‘Sense and Sensibility’?
English Literature.exp:
Jane Austen (1775 – 1817): She is called an anti-romantic novelist in the Romantic age because of her stern attitude against youthful passion.
Major works: Pride and prejudice (1797), Sense and Sensibility (1798 – 98), Mansfield park, Emma, Persuasion etc.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture]

English Literature.question: ১৪) Robert Browning belongs to-
English Literature.exp:
Robert Browning (1812–1889): English poet of the Victorian age. He is famous for Dramatic Monologues.
His famous works: Dramatic Lyrics, Dramatist Personae, The Patriot, My Last Duchess, Andrea Del Sarto, The Pied Piper of Hamelin, The Ring and the Book, Rabbi Ben Ezra etc.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture and An ABC of English Literature, Dr M Mofizar Rahman.]

English Literature.question: ১৫) Who wrote the poem ‘Dover Beach’?
English Literature.exp:
Matthew Arnold is a Melancholic/Elegiac poet.
His famous books: The Study of Poetry, Literature and Dogma, Culture and Anarchy, Essays in Criticism.
His famous Elegy: Thyrsis, Rughby Chapel, Heine's Grave.
Famous poems: Dover Beach, Sohrab and Rustom, The Scholar Gypsy, Cromwell etc.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture and An ABC of English Literature, Dr M Mofizar Rahman.]

English Literature.question: ১৬) Who is the author of the book ‘Utilitarianism’?
English Literature.exp:
John Stuart Mill (1806-73): English philosopher, economist, and exponent of Utilitarianism.
Famous Books: On Liberty, Utilitarianism, The Subjection of Women.
[Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr. M Mofizar Rahman]

English Literature.question: ১৭) “Water, water, everywhere,/ Nor any drop to drink” is a quotation of-
English Literature.exp:
Among the many memorable lines from ‘The Rime of the ancient Mariner’ poem is an utterance in stanza nine: “Water, water, everywhere,/Nor any drop to drink.”
Other memorable lines:
-“He prayth best who loveth best,/All things both great and small.”
- “Alone, alone, all, all alone,/Alone on a wide wide sea.”
[Source: LiveMCQ Lecture and Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ১৮) Charles Dickens is a great-
English Literature.exp:
Charles Dickens is the greatest novelist of the Victorian Period.
Famous novel of Charles Dickens: Oliver Twist, A Tale of Two Cities, Great Expectations, David Copperfield, Our Mutual Friend, The Christmas Carol, The Bleak House, The Old Curiosity Shop, The Pickwick Papers, Hard Times, The Mystery of Edwin Drood, Little Dorrit, The Battle of Life etc.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture and An ABC of English Literature, Dr M Mofizar Rahman]

English Literature.question: ১৯) Who translated the 'Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam' into English?
English Literature.exp:
Edward FitzGerald(1809-1883): English writer. He translated the 'Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam' into English from Persian.
Omar Khayyam chiefly known to English-speaking readers through the translation of a collection of his robāʿīyāt (“quatrains”) in The Rubáiyát of Omar Khayyám (1859), by the English writer Edward FitzGerald.
[Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr M Mofizar Rahman and Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ২০) Which of the following is a novel written by Thomas Hardy?
English Literature.option3: গ) A Pair of Blue Eyes
English Literature.exp:
Thomas Hardy was a Pessimistic Novelist.
His famous novels are Tess of the d'Urbervilles, Far From the Madding Crowd, The Return of the Native, The Poor Man and The Lady, The Mayor of Casterbridge, Jude the Obscure, The Trumpet Major, A Pair of Blue Eyes, Under the Greenwood Tree etc.
‘Catherine: A Story’ is a novel written by William Makepeace Thackery.
‘Great Expectations’ and ‘Hard Times’ novel by Charles Dickens.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture.]

English Literature.question: ২১) ‘Vanity Fair’ is a famous-
English Literature.exp:
William Makepeace Thackery was an Indian born British novelist.
His famous novels: Vanity Fair, The Virginians: A Tale of the Last Century, Catherine: A Story, The Newcomes.
[Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ Lecture.]

English Literature.question: ২২) Who is the writer of 'Treasure Island'?
English Literature.exp:
R.L. Stevenson(1850-1894): Scottish essayist, poet, and author of fiction and travel books, best known for his novels Treasure Island (1881), Kidnapped (1886), Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde (1886), and The Master of Ballantrae (1889).
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ২৩) What is the pen-name/pseudonym of Emily Bronte?
English Literature.exp:
Emily Brontë was an English novelist and poet who wrote a single novel, Wuthering Heights (1847), a highly imaginative work of passion and hate set on the Yorkshire moors. The novel was published in 1847 under the pseudonym Ellis Bell.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ২৪) Tennyson’s ‘In Memoriam’ is-
English Literature.exp:
Lord Alfred Tennyson was a represented/ Lyric poet of the Victorian Age.
His famous elegy: ‘In Memoriam’.
His famous poems: Oenone, Ulysses, Lotus Eaters, Locksley Hall, Tears Idle Tears, Tithonus, The Two Voices, The Lady of Shalott, Vision of Sin, Morte D'Arthur etc.
Famous comedies: The Falcon, Queen Mary, Harold.
[Source: LiveMCQ Lecture and Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ২৫) Who is the author of the novel 'Jane Eyre'?
English Literature.exp:
Charlotte Brontë, pseudonym Currer Bell (1816-1855): She is a Victorian novelist.
His famous novels: The Professor, Jane Eyre, Shirley, Villette etc.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture and An ABC of English Literature, Dr M Mofizar Rahman.]

English Literature.question: ২৬) Who was known as a leader of the ‘Oxford Movement’?
English Literature.exp:
John Henry Cardinal Newman was a leader of the 'Oxford Movement'.
His famous books: The Idea of University(Poem), Loss and Gain(Novel).
[Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ Lecture.]

English Literature.question: ২৭) Which novel was written by Alexander Dumas?
English Literature.exp:
Alexandre Dumas (1802–1870): He is a French writer.
His notable works: The Three Musketeers (Novel), The Gold Thieves (Drama), Twenty Years After(Novel) etc.
‘Silas Marner’ novel written by George Eliot and ‘Loss and Gain’ novel written by Cardinal Newman.
[Source: Live MCQ lecture.]

English Literature.question: ২৮) One of the four mentioned below is not a Victorian period poet. Who is he/she?
English Literature.exp:
John Keats(1795-1821) English Romantic lyric poet. He is called the Poet of Beauty and also Poet of Sensuousness.
His famous books: Endymion, Hyperion, Lamia.
Famous Poems: Ode to a Nightingale, Ode to Autumn, The Eve of St. Agnes, Ode to Psyche etc.
[Source: Live MCQ lecture.]

English Literature.question: ২৯) Who is the author of the novel ‘Adam Bede’?
English Literature.exp:
George Eliot, pseudonym of Mary Ann Evans (1819-1880): English Victorian novelist who developed the method of psychological analysis characteristic of modern fiction.
Her major works include- Adam Bede (1859), The Mill on the Floss (1860), Silas Marner (1861), Middlemarch (1871–72), and Daniel Deronda (1876).
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৩০) Which of the following is a novel written by Oscar Wilde?
English Literature.option2: খ) A woman of No Importance
English Literature.option3: গ) The Picture of Dorian Gray
English Literature.option4: ঘ) The Importance of Being Earnest
English Literature.exp:
Oscar Wilde(1854-1900): He was an Irish poet, novelist and dramatist.
His famous books and plays are- The Importance of Being Earnest(Comic play), A woman of No Importance(Comic play), An Ideal Husband(Play), The Picture of Dorian Gray(Novel), Lady Windermere's Fan etc.
[Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ Lecture.]

English Literature.question: ৩১) ‘The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn’ is a/an-
English Literature.option2: খ) fairy tales by Christian Unlerson
English Literature.option3: গ) adventure novel by Alexander Dumas
English Literature.option4: ঘ) short story by Edgar Allan Poe
English Literature.exp:
Samuel Langhorne Clemens is the real name of Mark Twain.
His famous works: Life on the Mississippi, The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn(Novel), The Adventures of Tom Sawyer(Novel).
[Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ Lecture.]

English Literature.question: ৩২) ‘Mr. Kurtz’ is a fictional character of-
English Literature.exp:
Joseph Conrad(1857-1924):
English novelist and short-story writer of Polish descent, whose works include the novels Lord Jim : A Tale (1900), Nostromo (1904), and The Secret Agent (1907) and the short story “Heart of Darkness” (1902).
‘Mr. Kurtz’ fictional character, the manager of a trading station in the interior of the Belgian Congo, in Joseph Conrad’s “Heart of Darkness” (1902).
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica and Live MCQ Lecture.]

English Literature.question: ৩৩) Who is the author of the drama ‘Arms and the Man’?
English Literature.exp:
George Bernard Shaw (1856-1950): He was a modern dramatist, famous for his 'drama of ideas'.
G B. Shaw’s famous plays:
Man and Superman, Candida, Arms and The Man, St. Joan of Arc, Man of Destiny, Press cuttings, You Never Can Tell, The Devil's Discipline, the Doctor's Dilemma, Major Barbara, Pygmalion, the Apple Cart, Caesar and Cleopatra, Beauty's duty etc.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica and Live MCQ Lecture.]

English Literature.question: ৩৪) ‘Riders to the Sea’ is-
English Literature.option1: ক) a poem by Lord Byron
English Literature.option2: খ) a play by J.M. Synge
English Literature.option3: গ) a novel by D.H. Lawrence
English Literature.option4: ঘ) a short story by Maugham
English Literature.exp:
J.M. Synge(1871-1909): In full John Millington Synge, leading figure in the Irish literary renaissance.
His famous works: Riders to The Sea (one act play), In the Shadow of the Glen, The Well of the Saints, The Playboy of the Western World, The Tinker's Wedding.
[Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr M Mofizar Rahman]

English Literature.question: ৩৫) ‘Daisy Miller’ is a novel written by -
English Literature.exp:
Henry James(1843-1916): He is an American born English writer.
‘Daisy Miller’ novel by Henry James, published in Cornhill Magazine in 1878 and published in book form in 1879.
Jame's other novels: The Portrait of a Lady (1881), The Bostonians (1886), The Ambassadors (1903), The Wings of the Dove(1902), Washington Square etc.
[Source: An ABC of English Literature and Live MCQ lecture.]

English Literature.question: ৩৬) Rudyard Kipling’s ‘Kim’ is a-
English Literature.exp:
Rudyard Kipling(1865-1936): English short-story writer, poet, and novelist. He is the first British to win a Nobel prize in 1907.
‘Kim’ novel by Rudyard Kipling, published in 1901.
His other famous work: The Jungle Book (Short Story), Plain Tales from The Hills, The Tomb of His Ancestors, The Mark of the Beast etc.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture and Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৩৭) Among the following, who is famous for “Symbolism and Mysticism”?
English Literature.exp:
William Butler Yeats (1865 – 1939):
- Irish dramatist, poet and critic.
- He is famous for his use of “Symbolism and Mysticism”.
- He wrote the preamble of Tagore's ''Song Offerings'' in 1912, which later got nobel prize in 1913.
- W.B Yeats got the Nobel prize in 1923.
Major Works:
Poems: The wild swans at coole, The Tower, The Winding Stair and Other poems, The Resurrection, The Second Coming, The Cat and the Moon, Byzantium, The Lake Isle of Innisfree, Among School Children, The Lord of Harts, falling of leaves, A prayer for My Daughter, When You Are Old.
Drama: The countess Cathleen, Cathleen in Houlihan.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica and Live MCQ Lecture]

English Literature.question: ৩৮) Which of the following writers has won the Nobel Prize in Literature?
English Literature.exp:
Bertrand Arthur William Russell(1872–1970):
British philosopher, logician, and social reformer, founding figure in the analytic movement in Anglo-American philosophy, and recipient of the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1950.
His notable works: Principia Mathematica, Mysticism and Logic and Other Essays, Why I Am Not a Christian, The Problems of Philosophy (1911), The Analysis of Mind (1921), The Analysis of Matter (1927), On Education (1926), Marriage and Morals (1929), The Conquest of Happiness (1930), A History of Western Philosophy (1945), Human Knowledge: Its Scope and Limits (1948), etc.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৩৯) Who wrote the short story 'The Gift of the Magi'?
English Literature.exp:
O’ Henry, pseudonym of William Sydney Porter(1862-1910): American short-story writer.
His famous short stories are:
- The Gift of the Magi
- Heart of the West
- The Voice of the City
- The Gentle Grafter
- The Ransom of Red Chief etc.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৪০) D.H. Lawrence’s ‘The Virgin and the Gypsy’ is a -
English Literature.exp:
D.H. Lawrence(1885-1930): In full David Herbert Lawrence. English author of novels, short stories, poems, plays, essays, travel books, and letters.
His novels: Sons and Lovers (1913, The Virgin and the Gypsy, The Rainbow (1915), Women in Love (1920), The White Peacock, Lady Chatterley's Lover, Aaron’s Rod, Kangaroo etc.
His famous short stories: The Rocking Horse Winner, The Captain Doll, The Labybird, The Price, The Fox.
His plays: Touch and Go, The Married Man.His Poems: The White Horse, Birds Beasts and Flowers.
Source: Live MCQ Lecture and Encyclopaedia Britannica

English Literature.question: ৪১) Who wrote ‘For Whom the Bell Tolls’?
English Literature.exp:
Ernest Hemingway is an American novelist. He was awarded the Nobel prize in 1954 for literature.
‘For Whom the Bell Tolls’ novel by Ernest Hemingway, published in 1940.
His famous novels are- The Old Man and The Sea, A Farewell to Arms, The Sun Also Rises, Death in the Afternoon, To Have and Have not.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture.]

English Literature.question: ৪২) ‘Everyone thinks of changing the world, but no one thinks of changing himself.’was quoted by-
English Literature.exp:
Leo Tolstoy(1828-1910):
Russian author Leo Tolstoy is considered a master of realistic fiction and one of the world’s greatest novelists, especially known for his two longest works, War and Peace (1865–69) and Anna Karenina (1875–77), which are commonly regarded as among the finest novels ever written.
‘Everyone thinks of changing the world, but no one thinks of changing himself.’was quoted from The Power Of Darkness by Leo Tolstoy.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica & The Power Of Darkness by Leo Tolstoy]

English Literature.question: ৪৩) ‘The Luncheon’ is a/an-
English Literature.exp:
William Somerset Maugham(1874 – 1935): English novelist, playwright and story writer.
Works:
Novels: Of Human Bondage, The Sacred Flames, The Razor’s Edge, Cakes and Ale, the Magician, The Moon and Sixpence, Lady Frederick.
Play: The Land of Promise.
Short Stories: The Ant and the Grasshopper, the Luncheon.
[Source: Britannica and Live MCQ Lecture.]

English Literature.question: ৪৪) Virginia Woolf’s ‘A Room of One’s Own’ is a-
English Literature.exp:
Virginia woolf(1882–1941):
She was a British female novelist. She is famous for ‘Presentation of inner realities’.
Her famous novels are: The Voyage Out (first novel), To the Lighthouse, Mrs. Dalloway, Orlando: A biography etc.
Her most famous essay was ‘A Room of One’s Own (1929)’.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture and Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৪৫) Who is the author of the play 'Exiles'?
English Literature.exp:
James Joyce is famous for his Narrative Technique known as 'Stream of Consciousness'.
His famous works: Exiles (Play), Ulysses(Novel), A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man, Chamber Music.
‘The Exiles: A Novel’ is written by Christina Baker Kline.
[Source: Britannica.]

English Literature.question: ৪৬) ‘Adela’ is a character from E.M. Forster’s novel-
English Literature.option4: ঘ) A Room with a View
English Literature.exp:
E.M. Forster(1879-1970):In full Edward Morgan Forster. British novelist, essayist, and social and literary critic.
His fame rests largely on his novels Howards End (1910) and A Passage to India (1924).
Foster's other works:
- Aspects of Novel
- Where Angels Fear to Tread
- The Longest Journey
- A Room With a View
- The Celestial Omnibus(Collection of short stories).
E.M. Forster's famous Novel 'A Passage to India'. Characters of 'A Passage to India' novel: Dr. Aziz, Miss Adela, Rony Hislop, Stella Moore.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture and Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৪৭) ‘Things Fall Apart’ is a literary work by-
English Literature.exp:
Chinua Achebe(1930-2013):
-One of the world's most widely recognized and praised Nigerian novelists.
-Chinua Achebe wrote some of the most extraordinary works of the 20th century.
Things Fall Apart (1958), Achebe’s first novel, concerns traditional Igbo life at the time of the advent of missionaries and colonial government in his homeland.
His other Notable works: No Longer at Ease, Arrow of God, A Man of the People, Anthills of the Savannah.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৪৮) Who is the creator of the character ''Tess''?
English Literature.exp:
This character is from ‘Tess of the D'Urbervilles’, a novel by Thomas Hardy.
Thomas Hardy was a Pessimistic Novelist and Poet.
His other famous novels are-
A Pair of Bluest Eyes, Under the Greenwood Tree, The Return of the Native, The Mayor of Casterbridge.
Poems: The Blinded Bird, The voice, After a journey.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture]

English Literature.question: ৪৯) “Nothing is so good as it seems beforehand.” was stated by-
English Literature.exp:
‘Nothing is so good as it seems beforehand.’- Silas Marner by George Eliot.
Other famous quotation: ‘One must be poor to know the luxury of giving.’-Middlemarch.
‘Our deeds determine us, as much as we determine our deeds.’-Adam Bede.

English Literature.question: ৫০) ‘The Everlasting Mercy’ is a long narrative poem by-
English Literature.exp:
John Masefield(1878-1967):
-He is a British poet.
-Best known for his poems of the sea, ‘Salt-Water Ballads’ (1902, including “Sea Fever” and “Cargoes”), and for his long narrative poems, such as ‘The Everlasting Mercy’ (1911).
His other notable works: Dauber, Reynard the Fox.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]
